text: Coordinating long-running processes on top of distributed systems is one of the persistent hard problems in software.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: A process that runs across many steps can't count on finishing in one clean pass, since the machines running it may crash, stall, or drop connections.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: To handle this fragility, developers have often resorted to writing layers of retries, timeouts, and checkpointing to keep state alive across failures.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: However, this custom plumbing is often brittle, hard to maintain, and can break down at scale.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Temporal is an open-source platform built around an approach it calls durable execution.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Developers write a workflow as a straightforward sequence of steps, and the platform preserves its full state underneath, so the code can survive a crash and resume exactly where it left off.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: The underlying technology was created at Uber over a decade ago.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Since then, Temporal has become foundational infrastructure for AI and agent workloads, where long-running tools and agent loops need exactly this kind of durability.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Maxim Fatayev is a co-founder of Temporal.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: He returns to the show with Sean Falconer to discuss how durable execution works, why it's infrastructure rather than a framework, how it fits the non-deterministic world of AI agents,
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Its new capabilities and why Temporal's fully open source strategy is central to its moat.
